title: Diagonal component and strict generic component-count decrease in a smooth self-product
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty affine Noetherian integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme] which is normal, meaning every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $f:Y\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type with $Y$ nonempty and integral [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\eta$ and $\xi$ for the generic points of $S$ and $Y$, with residue fields $k(S)$ and $k(Y)$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-sc-function-field, def-weil-residue-field]. For a morphism $t:Z\to T$ with $T$ nonempty integral and with finite-type generic fibre, define $\rho_t(Z)$ to be the number of irreducible components of $Z\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k(T)}$, where $\overline{k(T)}$ is an algebraic closure [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $N=\rho_f(Y)$ and $W=Y\times_SY$, with first projection $\pi:W\to Y$ and diagonal $\Delta:Y\to W$. Then $N$ is a positive finite integer. The scheme $W$ is Noetherian and normal and has finitely many nonempty normal integral open-and-closed components $C_0,\ldots,C_m$. Exactly one of them, denoted $C_0$, contains $\Delta(Y)$. For every $i$, the morphism $\pi_i=\pi|_{C_i}:C_i\to Y$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and dominant (has dense image), and
$$\rho_{\pi_0}(C_0)=1,\qquad \sum_{i=0}^m\rho_{\pi_i}(C_i)=N,\qquad 1\leq\rho_{\pi_i}(C_i)<N\quad (i>0).$$
The generic fibre $(C_0)_\xi$ is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $\Delta$ factors through $C_0$ as a section of $\pi_0$. For every nonempty affine open $B\subseteq Y$, the schemes $C_{i,B}=C_i\times_Y B$ are nonempty normal integral open subschemes of $C_i$, their maps to $B$ are smooth separated of finite type, and their geometric generic component counts are the same as those of $\pi_i$. The diagonal section restricts to $B\to C_{0,B}$. No surjectivity of $Y\to S$ or geometric integrality of its generic fibre is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.3(i)-(ii), with both factors Y and g=id_Y; positivity, sum and affine-open restrictions explicitly included; printed p.10 of March 31, 2026 version, read online. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The first projection $\pi:W\to Y$ is the base change of $f$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], first $Y$ and then $W$ are Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], first $Y$ and then $W$ are normal. Every open of $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Thus [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components] applies to $W$. Its components are nonempty normal integral clopen subschemes, pairwise disjoint and covering $W$, and there are finitely many of them.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles; descent.tex Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth; morphisms.tex Tags 01T6, 01VB; schemes.tex Tag 01KU

proof.text: Write the components as $C_i$. Since each inclusion $j_i:C_i\hookrightarrow W$ is open, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] makes $\pi_i=\pi j_i$ smooth. It is also a closed immersion: its underlying image is closed, and its structure-sheaf map is an isomorphism on that image and a surjection to zero off it [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $j_i$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and $\pi_i$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The diagonal of $\pi_i$ is the base change of the closed diagonal of $\pi$ along $C_i\times_Y C_i\to W\times_Y W$: a pair of points of $C_i$ equal in $W$ is the same point of $C_i$, with the same scheme-theoretic universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] it is closed, so $\pi_i$ is separated.

source.place: Tags 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), 01W5 (closed immersions proper); schemes.tex separated-diagonal base change

proof.text: Both $f$ and every $\pi_i$ are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], hence open maps by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Each has nonempty source and integral target. Its image is therefore a nonempty open of an irreducible space, hence dense and containing the target generic point [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sc-generic-point]. Thus $f$ is dominant, $\xi$ maps to $\eta$, and every $\pi_i$ is dominant with nonempty generic fibre. To justify the middle assertion explicitly, continuity gives $f(Y)\subseteq\overline{\{f(\xi)\}}$; since $f(Y)$ contains $\eta$, its closure is $S$, so $f(\xi)$ is the unique generic point $\eta$. No surjectivity is needed.

source.place: Tags 01VF, lemma-smooth-flat, and 01UA, lemma-fppf-open; elementary topology of an integral scheme

proof.text: Each $(C_i)_\xi$ is irreducible. Indeed [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies its topology with the subspace $\pi_i^{-1}(\xi)$. Lift two nonempty opens of this subspace to opens $U,V$ of $C_i$. They are nonempty and intersect because $C_i$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The nonempty open $U\cap V$ has nonempty open image under the open map $\pi_i$ from step 3; this image contains $\xi$, so the two fibre opens intersect. Nonemptiness was proved in step 3. This proves the irreducibility assertion directly from the definitions.

source.place: Tags 01K0 (definition-fibre), 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological); elementary subspace topology and step 3

proof.text: The nonempty continuous image $\Delta(Y)$ of the irreducible scheme $Y$ lies in exactly one member of the finite clopen partition from step 1: otherwise its intersections with a component and its clopen complement separate this irreducible image [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Relabel that member $C_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], $\Delta$ factors through $C_0$. The identities $\pi\Delta=\mathrm{id}_Y$, and hence $\pi_0\Delta=\mathrm{id}_Y$, follow from the two projection identities in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Base change gives a $k(Y)$-rational point $c$ of $(C_0)_\xi\subseteq W_\xi$. Since $(C_0)_\xi$ is irreducible by step 4 and clopen in $W_\xi$ (the fibre has its subspace topology by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]), it is exactly the connected component of $c$.

source.place: Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens; fibre-product projection identities and clopen partition topology

proof.text: The scheme $W_\xi$ is smooth of finite type over $k(Y)$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. For the point $c$ of step 5, the structure map and the rational point give field maps $k(Y)\to\kappa(c)\to k(Y)$ whose composite is the identity; injectivity identifies $\kappa(c)$ with $k(Y)$, a purely transcendental extension in zero variables. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-component-pure-transcendental] with $k=k(Y)$, $C=W_\xi$, $c=c$. Its connected component is precisely $(C_0)_\xi$ by step 5, so this generic fibre is geometrically integral. Consequently $\rho_{\pi_0}(C_0)=1$, by the definition of the count and [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 057K, connected component T in proof; varieties.tex Tags 04KV and 056T

proof.text: The geometric generic fibres of $f$ and of all $\pi_i$ are finite-type schemes over algebraically closed fields, by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. They are nonempty: the ordinary generic fibres are nonempty by step 3, and field extension preserves nonemptiness by [lem-sfb-field-extension-irreducible-components] together with [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. These two nodes also show that every nonempty one has an irreducible component. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], their numbers of irreducible components are positive finite integers. In particular $N$ and every $\rho_{\pi_i}(C_i)$ are positive finite.

source.place: Tags 01T4 and 01T6; varieties.tex Tag 04KX; topology.tex irreducible component covering

proof.text: By [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-component-count-base-change] applied to $f$ and the base change $Y\to S$, the number of geometric irreducible components of $W_\xi$ equals that of $Y_\eta$, namely $N$, since $f(\xi)=\eta$ by step 3. Base-changing the finite clopen partition of $W$ gives a finite clopen partition of its geometric generic fibre into the geometric generic fibres of $C_i\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]: the pieces are the inverse images of the original disjoint opens, and their complements are the unions of the other inverse images. Any irreducible subset lies in one piece: meeting two pieces separates it into complementary nonempty clopens. A maximal irreducible subset in a piece is maximal in the whole space, and conversely [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Therefore $\sum_i\rho_{\pi_i}(C_i)=N$. The $i=0$ summand is $1$ by step 6 and all other summands are positive by step 7, so for $i>0$ we have $1\leq\rho_{\pi_i}(C_i)\leq N-1<N$.

Let $B\subseteq Y$ be nonempty affine open. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $C_{i,B}=C_i\times_YB$ is the open subscheme $\pi_i^{-1}(B)$ of $C_i$. It is nonempty because the dense image of $\pi_i$ meets $B$. A nonempty open of an integral scheme is integral: it is irreducible by intersection of nonempty opens, and each of its affine opens is an affine open of $C_i$, with domain ring [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its local rings are those of $C_i$, so it is normal. Its map to $B$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The generic point $\xi$ belongs to $B$ and has the same residue field there [def-sc-generic-point]; the two generic fibres are canonically isomorphic because $(C_i\times_YB)\times_B\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)=C_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus their geometric generic counts agree. Base change of the section in step 5 gives the required section $B\to C_{0,B}$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-df7c15595 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's 9-step split (no new nodes) in full, with every cited statement. The statement is unchanged. I tested it on three cases. Y=S gives N=1. For a finite separable extension L/K, L⊗_K L=∏L_i with ρ_i=[L_i:L], so the sum is [L:K], ρ_0=1 and every other ρ_i is between 1 and N−1. A proper open Y⊂S is not surjective onto S and still works, so no surjectivity hypothesis is hidden. Steps: S1 gets smoothness, separatedness, finite type, Noetherianity and normality from base change and ascent, then the clopen normal integral components from Tag 0357; its hypothesis that every qc open has finitely many components holds because open subschemes of a Noetherian scheme are Noetherian. S2: j_i is a clopen closed immersion, so π_i is finite type by composition, and it is separated because the diagonal square along the monomorphism j_i is cartesian. S3: smooth, hence flat and lfp, hence open, so each map is dominant and f(ξ)=η. S4: the generic fibre of an open map from an irreducible space is irreducible; the argument is elementary and correct. S5: the irreducible Δ(Y) lies in exactly one clopen piece and gives a k(Y)-rational point c in (C_0)_ξ, which is the connected component of c. S6: 057K applies with r=0 (κ(c)=k(Y)), so (C_0)_ξ is geometrically integral and ρ_0=1. S7: the geometric generic fibres are finite type over a field, hence Noetherian and nonempty, so 1≤ρ<∞. S8: 0556 with t′=ξ gives n_{W/Y}(ξ)=n_{Y/S}(η)=N; components are additive over a finite clopen partition, so the sum is N, which gives the bound. The 055F connected-component node (lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change) is correctly not used. S9: C_{i,B} is the open preimage π_i^{-1}(B), nonempty because ξ∈B, and the generic fibres agree because Spec k(Y)→Y factors through B. Batch 5: I walked the closures of lem-trf-smooth-component-pure-transcendental (282 nodes) and lem-trf-geometric-fibre-component-count-base-change (70 nodes). Neither reaches a trace-formula, Poincaré or purity node. Both are general scheme geometry, outside both assumptions, so I accept them as the tool_uses recorded in split_report. No non-trf node states 0556 or 057K, and no node duplicates the item. The Guo PDF is absent locally (WANTED), so the source could not be reread here. Advisory only: step 5 could also cite lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, and step 6 could cite def-pc-geometrically-irreducible.
